review.expectedBehavior: A Node HTTP request timing out with timeoutErrorMessage configured rejects with the hard-coded timeout text instead of the configured message.
review.sourceCause: The HTTP timeout callback constructs AxiosError with a literal duration message and never reads config.timeoutErrorMessage; the XHR adapter does honor it.
review.matchingCriteria: Identify the Node HTTP timeout path, the ignored custom message option, and the incorrect emitted error message. A generic timeout warning is insufficient.
review.negativeControl: Without a custom message, retain the normal timeout message and timeout error code; XHR already honors the option and must not be accused of the same omission.

review.sourceCause: Both 3-backtick and 4-backtick extraction regexes require bare LF directly after the info string and before the closing fence; CR remains and prevents the match.
review.matchingCriteria: Identify unwrapMdxCodeBlocks, CRLF versus LF, the regex boundary assumption and the effect on embedded MDX. A claim that all Markdown parsing fails is too broad.
review.negativeControl: Existing LF-wrapped blocks and 3/4-backtick support remain valid; do not report LF blocks as broken or demand arbitrary fence lengths despite the explicit scope comment.

review.expectedBehavior: Range(0,10).filter(x => true).slice(-2).toArray() returns the full range rather than [8,9] when filter has left sequence size unknown.
review.sourceCause: Negative indices with undefined size pass through bitwise ToInt32 coercion in resolveIndex, turning NaN into 0 before sliceFactory tests for NaN. Its cache-and-retry branch does not run.
review.matchingCriteria: Connect unknown size after filtering, negative slice index resolution, the ineffective NaN guard and wrong slice result. Reporting a generic performance issue does not match.
review.negativeControl: Known-size Range without filter and positive-begin slices are controls; do not call every slice broken or claim the library mutates the original collection.

review.expectedBehavior: Cloning Line, Mesh or Points retains the exact same material array object, so replacing/pushing an element through the clone also changes the original material list.
review.sourceCause: Each copy method directly assigns this.material = source.material; Object3D.clone delegates to copy.
review.matchingCriteria: Identify aliasing of the material ARRAY container on cloning, with at least one concrete mutation consequence. Retain sharing of individual Material objects. Issue-level hit needs one valid affected path; full occurrence coverage requires all three.
review.negativeControl: Sharing a single Material object and the individual materials inside a copied array is intended. Recommending unconditional deep cloning of every material fails the oracle.

review.expectedBehavior: Initial rendering of a progress element with numeric value 0 can leave its value attribute absent, so the DOM treats it as indeterminate.
review.sourceCause: The value update is skipped when newProps.value equals dom.value, although a progress DOM property defaults to zero even without the determining attribute.
review.matchingCriteria: Tie the property equality shortcut to progress value 0, the missing value attribute and determinate/indeterminate behavior. Claiming zero children never render does not match.
review.negativeControl: Do not generalize to all zero values or say numeric zero children must disappear. Normal text zero and ordinary controlled inputs are separate behaviors.
